edges.effect_quant: Dose-response meta-analyses backed by prospective cohorts suggest a small average effect that is directionally consistent but not dramatic.
edges.mechanism: This early-life or prenatal exposure may shape Childhood neurodevelopment through developmental programming, microbiome establishment, immune maturation, or nutrient sufficiency during sensitive windows. Timing matters because the same exposure can be much more consequential in infancy or pregnancy than later in life.
edges.summary: In children with prenatal exposure, dose-response meta-analyses backed by prospective cohorts suggest that pesticide exposure during pregnancy tracks with adverse shifts in childhood neurodevelopment. Most disagreement in the literature is about size, subgroup sensitivity, or dose threshold rather than about whether the relationship exists at all.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.

evidence.notes: Early Life Exposure in Mexico to ENvironmental Toxicants (ELEMENT) Project.

evidence.citation: SapbamrerR et al 2019 Environ Sci Pollut Res Int
